newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear CEO says $4.30-$4.50 FY96 EPS reasonable.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear CEO says $4.30-$4.50 FY96 EPS reasonable.

text.p: Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co chief executive officer Samir Gibara said Monday that analysts' earnings estimates for 1996 of $4.30-$4.50 a share versus $4.02 in 1995 are "reasonable" depending on the General Motors Corp strike in Canada and other factors.

The GM strike has so far cost the Akron, Ohio-based tiremaker $1.5 million in income but "we will more than offset that from other operations in North America and around the world," Gibara said in a telephone interview.

Asked about First Call's estimate range, Gibara said, "It sounds reasonable to me (depending on the strike's duration and other factors)." Goodyear is the largest tire supplier to domestic automakers, said Gibara, who is also chairman.

Goodyear earlier reported third quarter earnings of $1.09 a share versus $1.03 in the 1995 third quarter. It was the company's 22nd consecutive quarter-to-previous-year-quarter improvement in net income from operations, which rose eight percent from the 1995 third quarter, he said.

Sales were $3.27 billion versus $3.31 billion in the 1995 third quarter due to planned low tire sales to North American automakers, to competitive pricing on North American replacement tires and to currency translation, Goodyear said.
Gibara said the currency impact was $40 million for the quarter and $150 million in the first nine months of 1996.
Lower tire sales to North American automakers were by design, as the company has said previously, Gibara said.

While continuing to be a major supplier to Ford Motor Co Chrysler Corp, GM and "transplant" operations of overseas automakers, Goodyear has exited some smaller accounts and focused on the more profitable and less cyclical replacement tire market, he said.
Replacement tire sales in the U.S. increased, bringing U.S. tire unit sales even with 1995 levels, he said. Worldwide replacement tire sales were also up, the company said.
Gibara said gross margins improved and business expenses as a percent of sales declined in the quarter.
"Overall it was a very rewarding performance due to the continued implementation of our strategic plan as shared with the financial community a year ago," he said.
New products remain a key part of Goodyear's strategy, Gibara said. Its new Infinitred tire "is selling very well" and the company recently unveiled two lines of winter tires in Europe, he said.

Goodyear is considering closing one Ohio engineered products plant, he said. The St. Mary's, Ohio, plant's 650 workers approved a labor settlement but their union, the United Steelworkers of America, have not done so, he said, adding that Goodyear needs the new settlement to be competitive.
